analysis.title: Mike Wilson: Market Bad Breadth "Must Be Resolved One Way Or Another" And It All Hinges On Bond Vol
key_insights: Morgan Stanley's Mike Wilson says the gap between index price (just below all-time highs) and market breadth must close, and the path depends on bond volatility. If bond vol stays high, breadth and price meet in the middle over the next month, followed by a strong year-end. If bond vol subsides sooner, breadth catches up to the index and both rise in the near term.
51% of Russell 3000 members have fallen 20% or more since June, up from more than 40% a week earlier. The S&P 500 forward P/E is near 19x, matching the March low reached during the Iran conflict.
96% of semiconductor stocks have had a 20%+ drawdown since June and 69% are down 40% or more. Autos are at 71% and Software at 75%. Banks are at 4%.

Wilson frames the losers as classic early-cycle winners (Semis, Autos) that outperformed from the April 2025 trough through June 2026. Morgan Stanley called the peak in earnings revisions breadth for those names in June, and he sees the Fed's hawkish pivot as another signal of the move from early to mid cycle, with quality beginning to lead.

S&P 500 EPS revisions breadth is 25% versus 7% for the Russell 2000, and median stock EPS growth is in the mid-teens. The index has been flat since early June because multiples absorbed the shock, not because earnings stalled.

Wilson views higher crude and especially refined product prices as an inflation risk more than a growth risk, because current earnings growth differs from the setups that preceded past energy-driven recessions.

Wilson has flagged 4.50% on the 10Y as the level where equity rate sensitivity begins. The 10Y crossed it in May and the S&P forward P/E has been falling since. The 10Y is above 5% and was 5.25% on Friday, erasing the entire post-payrolls rally.

The share of S&P 500 stocks above their 200-day moving average rose from 59% in late May to about 75% over the summer, then fell to 49%. Wilson attributes the break to Jackson Hole (a more hawkish Fed path being priced), not oil.

Since late August the rise in yields reflects the Fed's hawkish pivot against a strong growth backdrop, which Wilson says is not bad for equities overall even if it affects leadership. He says the breadth/S&P divergence must reconcile before the bull market fully resumes.
Wilson's chart annotation puts the breadth/price spread at 12% in SPX terms, to be resolved one way or another.

Goldman's Lee Coppersmith (Sep 21) said fewer than 30% of S&P stocks were above their 50-day average, Goldman's Sentiment Indicator was -0.9 (lowest in over a year), and AAII bears rose 14 points to 53.3%.

Goldman's Peter Callahan (Sep 28) said the median S&P stock trades 16% below its 52-week high, with breadth at its lowest since the Dot-Com Bubble. The cap-weighted S&P beat equal-weight in 18 of 21 sessions.

Goldman and Morgan Stanley agree the fundamentals are intact. S&P EPS grew 51% y/y in Q2, forward P/E fell from about 23x to about 19x, and Goldman's 12-month target of 8,700 assumes little multiple expansion.

The 2-year yield is 4.89%, up nearly 60bps since Jackson Hole, where Warsh said inflation needed to fall 'fast enough.' September's hike reinforced that reaction function. Wilson thinks the bond market has moved to an overly hawkish near-term posture, since August CPI upside was concentrated in a few categories, and the term premium remains well behaved.

Wilson says the market may be assuming too many hikes while misjudging Warsh's willingness to use the balance sheet to fund deficits or stabilize financial conditions. He expects Warsh to provide liquidity if necessary, but markets may test his resolve first.

The MOVE index is above 100 while the VIX is under 15. Whether and when bond vol spills into equity vol determines how the breadth/index divergence resolves. ZeroHedge notes the spillover is already visible in credit (HY VIX).

ZeroHedge's own arithmetic (not Wilson's): a full catch-down of the index to breadth would put the S&P near 6,800, and a meet-in-the-middle outcome implies a roughly 6% pullback to about 7,300. Wilson's prior risk scenario was 7,100 and his 12-month bear case is 5,900.
Morgan Stanley's 2026 S&P EPS base case is $339 versus bottom-up consensus of $361, about 6% below the Street.

Positioning: stay with large-cap quality, particularly asset-light names with improving EPS revisions, favoring high free cash flow yield, low accruals and sales per employee. If the index falls to finish the multi-month correction under the surface, add riskier stocks over the next month.

Michelle Weaver's sixth AI mapping of about 3,600 stocks supports the enabler-to-adopter rotation. Consensus expects high-materiality AI Adopters to deliver 4.6% EBIT margin expansion in 2025-26, but the advantage fades in out-year estimates. Adopter NTM EPS is up about 70% over two years (Enablers more than doubled), and the median Adopter trades at 18x forward versus 22x for Enablers.

Companies where AI is core to the thesis have outperformed those where it is merely significant by 107%. Businesses where AI is a core threat have underperformed those facing moderate disruption by about 161%.

sector_views.rationale: Favored in the mid-cycle framework, especially names with improving EPS revisions, high free cash flow yield, low accruals and high sales per employee.
96% of semiconductor stocks have had a 20%+ drawdown since June. Wilson treats them as early-cycle winners handing off leadership, with riskier stocks to be added after any index decline.

tension_points.bull_case: Earnings are absorbing valuation compression in a mid-cycle handoff, with S&P EPS revisions breadth at 25%, median stock EPS growth in the mid-teens, and a well-behaved term premium. If bond vol subsides, breadth catches up to the index and both rise.
tension_points.bear_case: A 12% spread between breadth and the index must close. If bond vol stays high, the index meets breadth halfway, which ZeroHedge's math puts near 7,300 (about 6% lower), with a full catch-down near 6,800. Goldman notes breadth collapses have preceded larger drawdowns over 6-12 months.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Bond vol (MOVE above 100) spilling over into equity vol, or the 10Y holding above 5%, would favor the bearish path of the index meeting breadth.
